$comment: P69 (lane `cs`, D-C-A-READ-THROUGH-AN-ADDRESS-CONSTANT-IN-A-STATIC-INITIALIZER-IS-REFUSED): a static initializer may read THROUGH a pointer whose value is an address constant when the object it lands in is const (or a string literal) and its value is a constant — `*p`, `p[i]`, `p->m`. DSS refused all of them with H_StaticInitializerNotFolded: its evaluator read an element or member of a constant VALUE only, never through an address. The exit code is a bitmask of the reads that did not fold (1 `s[0]` of a const pointer to a string literal, 2 `p[1]` of a const pointer to a const array, 4 `*p` of `a + 1`, 8 `*(a + 1)`, 16 `*p` into a const char array, 32 `*"*"`, 64 `*p` of `&s.b` beside `s.a`, 128 `p->b` of a pointer to a const structure, 256 a block-scope const pointer read in a static local). MEASURED 2026-09-30 through `dssharness run probe-reference-cc`, this file: clang 18.1.3 at -std=c17 -pedantic-errors and -std=c2x builds and runs 42 (run 20260930-235647-c544acc1); gcc 13.3.0 refuses (it folds only `*&k`) and MSVC 19.51 refuses (C2099, run 20260930-235710-78f93967) — one working reference makes each read required. Every operand comes from argc. The release arm is REPORT-ONLY: the reads are folded data either way.
